description: Gaia GPS PDF export ('Gaia Topo (feet)', 2 mi scale bar), Giant's Castle / Mount Durnford / Thaba-Putsoa, uKhahlamba-Drakensberg (KwaZulu-Natal / Lesotho). Same page layout as fixtures/gaia-langalibalele: ONE north-up Web Mercator RGB raster (native.png, 1118x791) placed with '806.4 0 0 561.6 18. 15.68 cm', so map.jpg (300 dpi) is 1.59 % anisotropic (3.0054 x 2.9583 page px per native px); the legend band covers the bottom 35.5 native rows. Truth measured independently of the MapMe core: native px -> Web Mercator is an isotropic, axis-aligned affine, the consensus (mean scale, mean centre) of three estimates: (1) hillshade_terrarium: the map's hillshade against a Terrarium z13 hillshade (NCC over translation, scale and light; best light from 315 deg, 66 deg up), (2) hillshade_copernicus: the same against Copernicus GLO-30 on a z14 Mercator grid, (3) contour_layer_terrarium: the contour lines alone (160 ft interval), by the phase coherence of the Terrarium elevation at the contour pixels modulo 48.768 m. They agree with the consensus within 0.12-0.35 native px at the truth points (scale spread 0.015 %; the anisotropic fits are square to 0.04 %): the truth is good to about +-0.4 native px (+-9 m). Checks: local translations of 12 windows against each DEM (rms 0.3 px), summit icons against DEM summits, the printed scale bar (implies 22.947 m/px, the truth 22.990: the bar is 0.19 % short).
pixel_convention: continuous pixel coordinates: pixel (i, j) covers [i, i+1) x [j, j+1), its centre is (i + 0.5, j + 0.5); x right, y down (as the core: skeleton points sit at pixel centres +0.5)
mercator_convention: X = X0 + sx * x, Y = Y0 - sy * y (Web Mercator metres); pixel_to_mercator is the core's row-major 3x3

raster_placement_pt.note: content stream: "806.4 0 0 561.6 18. 15.68 cm /I0 Do"; top-down the raster spans x 18..824.4 pt, y 18..579.6 pt

checks.window_residuals_note: Each of 12 windows (4 x 3 over the map above the legend band; centres in native px) is registered alone against the DEM hillshade, translation only, holding the truth's scale and light: shift = the local offset in native px (0 where the truth fits exactly).
checks.alternative_fits_note: Each estimate's displacement from the truth (native px) at the 25 truth points: max and rms. m_per_px_scale is Web Mercator metres per native px.
checks.spot_heights_note: Summit icons (template match, centre of the triangle, native px) against the highest Copernicus GLO-30 cell within 210 m: icon_minus_summit_px under the truth, and the DEM summit elevation against the printed spot height (feet). Isolated summits sit within ~1-3 px; icons on the escarpment edge (Erskine, Bond, Potterill, Katana on map A) find a higher cell on the plateau behind them, and Gaia places the same summit's icon differently at different zooms (Mount Durnford: 3 px north of the summit on map A, 7 px on map B), so these check the identification and the scale, not the last pixel.
